decisive_items: invagination of the descending colon into the sigmoid colon consistent with intussusception
well-defined hypodense lesion measuring 4.6 × 3.4 cm with fat density in the sigmoid-colon wall protruding into the lumen
5 × 5 cm exophytic mass at the descending–sigmoid junction
response.rationale: CT explicitly demonstrates intussusception with a fat-density lead point; R6 captures the specific colorectal location and imaging pattern, while R4 is the generic term. Cancer/polyp candidates lack supporting evidence (normal CEA, fat density) and are secondary to the intussusception mechanism.

rejected.why: Generic intussusception without specifying colorectal site; less precise than R6.
CEA normal and CT fat density argue against cancer; mass is likely lead point, not primary malignancy.
Same as R3; normal CEA and fat density contradict malignancy.
Descriptive of mass but misses the definitive intussusception finding.
Polyp is too benign for 5 cm mass with intussusception; imaging favors lipoma-like lead point.
Mucopurulent discharge and erosions are nonspecific; no chronicity or extraintestinal features.
Diverticulitis would show inflammation, not intussusception; pain and discharge are explained by mass.
